chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, the Exalted, support him—informed us of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever performs ghusl from janabah and does not wash his head, then later decides to wash his head, he has no alternative but to repeat the ghusl."

So he عليه السلام clarified that whoever delays washing the head until after washing the rest of his limbs, it is obligatory upon him to wash the head and repeat washing the rest of the limbs. Were tartib not obligatory, he would not have required repeating the washing of the limbs. What has preceded already suffices regarding the obligation of tartib in both wudu (ablution) and ghusl, and we have cited here what further confirms that, and in it there is sufficiency, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.إِعَادَةِ الْغُسْلِ: repeating the ritual bath due to invalid sequence
key_terms.التَّرْتِيبَ: observing the prescribed order in ritual washing
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), mentioned alongside ghusl regarding order
key_terms.جَنَابَةٍ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: the head, whose washing must precede the rest in this ruling
key_terms.سَائِرِ الْأَعْضَاءِ: the rest of the body parts washed after the head
key_terms.غَسْلُ الرَّأْسِ: washing the head as a required component of ghusl

ai.seo_question: If someone washes the body before the head in ghusl from janabah, must the ghusl be repeated?
ai.summary: This report establishes that tartib in ghusl from janabah is obligatory: the head must be washed before the rest of the body. If a person omits the head and washes the remaining limbs first, he must wash the head and then repeat washing the rest of the body in the proper order.
